headline: Google has suspended its paid open-source bug bounty program because automated, mostly invalid AI-generated reports swamped it, and has promised an update in early 2027.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 2: a commentary repeat of the pause we carried on 5 Oct 2026, with no new fact.
importance_line: Researchers lose a paid route for reporting flaws in Google's open-source software while its other reward programs stay open, but this is a repeat of a story we carried on 5 Oct 2026, and Google has said only that it will update in the first quarter of 2027.
summary: BGR reports that Google has suspended its paid bug bounty program for open-source software (OSS VRP), which paid up to $31,337 for serious flaws, because the vast majority of automated submissions it receives are not valid, and that Google has promised an update in the first quarter of 2027 while its other reward programs stay open. The pause began on 1 Oct 2026 and this repeats the report we carried on 5 Oct 2026 from TechCrunch, which quoted Google.
notes: Read in full on BGR (commentary). Repeat of our 5 Oct 2026 entry (TechCrunch); BGR's claims about Curl, Intel, HackerOne and Linux are not used as fact.
